question.problem: In $2018$, Elena earned a salary of $$12,000.$ The following year, she earned $110%$ of the salary received in $2018.$ What was Elena's salary in $2019?$

current_example.problem: Marcus has a tank with a capacity of $1,500$ liters. He decides to buy a second tank whose capacity is $130 \%$ of the capacity of the first tank. What is the capacity of the second tank?
current_example.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we can use the following formula:

$$
\textrm{part}=  \textrm{percentage}\times \textrm{whole}
$$

In our case, the whole is the capacity of the first tank, which is $1,500$ liters. The percentage is $130 \%,$ and the part is the capacity of the second tank.

**Method 1**

First, we convert the percentage to a decimal:

$$
130 \% = 130 \div 100 = 1.3
$$

Applying our formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =130%\times 1,500 \\  & =1.3\times 1,500 \\  & =1,950.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the second tank has a capacity of $1,950$ liters.

**Method 2**

First, we convert the percentage to a fraction:

$$
130 \% = \dfrac{130}{100}
$$

Applying our formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =130%\times 1,500 \\  & =\frac{130}{100}\times 1,500 \\  & =130\times \frac{1,500}{100} \\  & =130\times 15 \\  & =1,950.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the second tank has a capacity of $1,950$ liters.
